Dynamic secret substitution for LLM privacy
Persistent autonomous 24/7 runtime (Autopilot)
Infrastructure code indexing for Terraform, Kubernetes, and Docker
Full session audit logging with replay capabilities

notIdealFor: Users without Docker availability or those who prefer a fully managed cloud PaaS that does not require self-hosting any local infrastructure management software.

verdict: Stakpak is a highly secure, privacy-focused alternative to generic coding agents, uniquely built for the high-stakes environment of production DevOps by prioritizing safety, auditing, and protection against unauthorized credential exposure.

name: OpenCode
pricingDetail: Go ($10/month), Go Plus ($40/month), Go Teams ($20/member/month)

Automations for recurring tasks via timers or cron schedules

name: Nanocoder

name: AI Prompt Architect

Interactive offline codebase map for visual exploration
CLI and VS Code extension for Git-change and file workflows

name: AgentBox
pricingDetail: Free (Open-source tool with no hosted pricing or tiers)

Secure host-side credential relay with approval shims
Native macOS tray app for management and dashboard access

name: Oh My Pi (omp)

name: BitFun

name: Atomic Agent

bestFor: Proof engineers and mathematicians requiring a persistent, verifiable system for formalizing complex mathematical statements using Lean 4.
notIdealFor: General users seeking a casual question-answering system or those without the technical background to manage a local Lean 4 development environment.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.0 (released October 2026) updated the installation process to make Lean/Mathlib optional by default and refreshed documentation for macOS and Linux packaging.
verdict: MathCode is a powerful, research-oriented tool that shifts AI math solving from one-off responses to a persistent, verifiable loop, though its steep technical requirements and strict platform constraints limit it to specialized use.

name: fx
pricingDetail: The fx software itself is free (Apache-2.0). Users pay for model inference based on their chosen credential: AI Gateway (pay-as-you-go per token), ChatGPT subscription (usage counts against existing plan limits), or Grok subscription (plan allowance or usage credits).
description: fx is a minimal, open-source coding agent CLI and harness written in Zig, optimized for high performance, embeddability, and portability across terminal, CI, and agent sandbox environments. It features a tiny native binary and supports multiple providers, acting as a modular core that can be extended via skills, MCP servers, and language SDKs.
keyFeatures: Native Zig binary with fast startup and low memory footprint
Embeddable core with Node.js and WebAssembly support
Model-agnostic connection to Vercel AI Gateway, ChatGPT, Grok, or custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints
Native support for MCP servers and custom skills
Subagent orchestration and workspace state capture
bestFor: Developers building automation pipelines, CI/CD integrations, disposable evaluation containers, or products that need to embed an agent harness.
notIdealFor: Users requiring Windows support, stable long-term release guarantees (currently v0.0.x with frequent breaking changes), or a mature, feature-rich daily driver experience similar to full-featured IDE assistants.
recentUpdates: Version 0.0.18 (2026-11-25) introduced more reliable subagents, faster shell command execution, and enhanced session management. Version 0.0.17 (2026-11-14) added concurrent subagent support, Vercel Token Pass integration, and performance improvements.
verdict: fx is a highly efficient, embeddable agent runner that excels in programmatic or resource-constrained environments, though its experimental status and lack of stability make it better suited for system components than as a primary daily coding assistant.

name: Zero
description: Zero is a Go-based terminal coding agent that runs locally on your machine, allowing you to bring your own AI model providers. It provides a secure, permission-gated environment for repository inspection, file editing, and command execution, with support for both interactive terminal use and headless CI automation.
keyFeatures: Supports 30+ model providers including local models via Ollama or LM Studio
OS-level sandboxing and permission-gated access for shell and file operations
Durable local session storage for searching, resuming, and forking history
Scriptable headless mode for CI/CD integration with structured stream-JSON I/O
Extensible architecture using MCP servers, plugins, skills, and subagents
bestFor: Developers who require a highly secure, locally-owned coding agent that can be used interactively in a TUI or programmatically in CI/CD pipelines.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a hosted cloud service or IDE-integrated assistant, as Zero is explicitly designed for the terminal and local execution.
recentUpdates: Version 0.14.0 released on 2026-11-17 added a durable memory tool, built-in companion pets, and various performance improvements and bug fixes for MCP and specialist agent functionality.
verdict: Zero is a powerful, privacy-focused tool for developers who want full control over their coding agent's autonomy, model selection, and data, offering a robust balance between interactive terminal convenience and automated headless utility.

name: Headlong
pricingDetail: Free (Apache License 2.0)
description: Headlong is an open-source agent microharness built on a Bash-centric architecture that enables persistent agency through a continuous, self-guided thought loop. It allows agents to maintain an inner monologue, manage their own projects, and operate autonomously 24/7.
keyFeatures: Persistent agency via recursive LLM loops
Tiered context compaction for long-term memory
Multi-user shared identity with a unified timeline
Docker-based sandboxing for secure command execution
Bash-centric, fully inspectable codebase
bestFor: Developers building autonomous, persistent agents for open-ended monitoring, research, and coordination tasks.
notIdealFor: Production environments requiring strict security boundaries, per-user session isolation, or predictable, low-cost billing.
recentUpdates: Recent October 2026 updates include refinements to the recap tool for handling model refusals, structural improvements for describing forbidden reply markup, and fixes to prevent the storage of blank memory summaries.
verdict: Headlong is an innovative, research-grade harness that provides a highly customizable, transparent framework for exploring autonomous agent logic, though it is not yet suitable for stable production use.

name: OB-1
pricingDetail: Free (Free), Hosted frontier (Paid subscription)
description: OB-1 is an open-source, terminal-based coding agent that provides persistent project memory and autonomous self-correction loops. It utilizes a unique provider-neutral design that allows developers to run tasks using a built-in free-models router, their own API keys, or a hosted frontier service.
keyFeatures: Embedded, keyless free-models router requiring no account or API keys
Autonomous self-correction loop that verifies code changes against project tests
Persistent local memory graph for tracking facts, revisions, and relationships
Fusion best-of-N orchestration for solving complex coding tasks
Provider-neutral architecture supporting OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, and custom endpoints
bestFor: Developers who work primarily in the terminal and require an ad-free, account-free starting point with the flexibility to switch between multiple LLM providers.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer a full GUI-based IDE experience with built-in features like real-time inline tab completion, as OB-1 is strictly a terminal-based CLI agent.
recentUpdates: Version 0.3.15 released on October 26, 2026, followed by 0.3.14 on October 25, 2026. Prior updates introduced Fusion mode, independent review commands, and deep search execution modes.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused coding agent that excels at verified task execution and avoiding vendor lock-in through its provider-neutral, terminal-first design.

name: Xirp
pricingDetail: Xirp desktop app (Free), Xirp + Portal Foundations (Free for 60 days, then contact sales)
description: Xirp is a desktop agentic development environment that acts as a vendor-neutral context layer for AI coding agents. It enables developers to manage multiple parallel agent sessions, maintain context across different tools, and integrate organizational knowledge via Spotify Portal.
keyFeatures: Parallel agent session management across Claude, Gemini, Codex, Pi, and Cursor
Portal Workspace integration for shared organizational context
Git worktree isolation for concurrent multi-tasking
Built-in cost alerting and usage monitoring
CLI tool for session interaction and transcript management
bestFor: macOS developers and teams already utilizing multiple AI coding agents who need to manage concurrent sessions and integrate organizational context.
notIdealFor: Developers on Windows or Linux, users of only a single agent on a single task, or organizations requiring open-source software.
recentUpdates: Released v0.67.0 on 2026-11-13 featuring improved minimap card layouts, restored session status visibility in the UI, and refined diff viewer behavior for binary files.
verdict: Xirp is a powerful, vendor-neutral orchestration layer that successfully solves context-switching fatigue for power users of AI coding agents, provided they work within the macOS ecosystem.

name: Kolkrabbi (kolk)
pricingDetail: The tool is open-source and free to use. It does not charge for its own service, though it integrates with your existing paid subscriptions (Claude Pro, ChatGPT Plus, GitHub Copilot) and third-party API providers like OpenRouter.
description: Kolkrabbi is a model-agnostic, open-source AI coding agent for the terminal that allows users to switch between multiple AI subscriptions and local models within a single session. It features a unique effort-based scaling system and provides a local dashboard to track model performance and costs without telemetry.
keyFeatures: Multi-subscription support (Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, OpenRouter, local models)
Three distinct modes: Chat, Code, and Agent orchestration
Effort-based scaling dial for model tier and task complexity
Local-only telemetry and cost tracking via stats.jsonl
Configurable permission tiers for file and shell access
bestFor: Developers who want a terminal-based AI coding agent that can switch between multiple LLM providers and local models while maintaining strict control over costs and privacy.
notIdealFor: Windows users, as the tool is primarily designed for macOS and Linux environments, and users looking for a cloud-synced or GUI-based experience.
recentUpdates: The tool has moved away from specific free-model presets like stealth/ox-alpha in favor of live free-model discovery via OpenRouter, and continues to refine its session checkpointing and sandbox security features.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused alternative to Claude Code that excels in flexibility and cost transparency, making it ideal for power users who want to manage their own AI toolchain.

name: FrontierAgent
pricingDetail: Free (open-source), user is responsible for model token costs via their own OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
description: FrontierAgent is an open-source agent runtime and terminal TUI designed for long-horizon research and file-based analysis. It provides two native workflows: a stateful ReAct mode for sequential tasks and an Agent Team mode that uses a coordinator to delegate work to parallel sub-agents.
keyFeatures: Native ReAct and Agent Team workflows
Task-scoped filesystem sandbox with fail-closed security
Live TUI task board and activity tracking
Local execution tracing, checkpointing, and /revert capability
Built-in evaluation suite for research and file-grounded benchmarks
bestFor: Developers and researchers performing multi-step, document-heavy analysis and those seeking a reference implementation for agent-team orchestration.
notIdealFor: Users requiring stable tagged releases, specialized software-engineering tools like LSP or deep git integration, or production-grade environments that demand hardened security beyond file-level sandboxing.
recentUpdates: Recent repository commits include fixes for shell process reaping, improved handling of quoted filenames, permission-level adjustments for command approvals, and new support for the Keenable search provider.
verdict: FrontierAgent is a highly capable and transparent research-oriented harness, but as a young, pre-release project that tracks the main branch, it is currently better suited for local experimentation and evaluation than for critical production workflows.

name: YYLO
pricingDetail: Free (no subscription fees or usage limits).
description: YYLO is a command-line orchestrator designed to manage multiple AI coding agents, repeatable workflows, and repository changes. It leverages Git worktrees to provide isolated workspaces and durable records for agent execution, validation evidence, and task status.
keyFeatures: Git-native task isolation using worktrees
Independent Ledger for task and record storage
Evidence-based benchmarking and evaluation
Repeatable, typed workflow orchestration
Centralized CLI management for multiple AI agents
bestFor: Developers and teams already using AI coding agents who need to orchestrate complex, multi-agent workflows with task isolation, durable documentation, and evidence-based validation.
notIdealFor: Users without an existing AI agent setup, those who require a graphical user interface (GUI), or teams that prefer not to work within a terminal environment.
recentUpdates: The v0.2.14 release (2026-11-04) allows controller upgrades even when historical task packages are missing and enables parsing of hydration YAML without requiring external PyYAML.
verdict: YYLO is a powerful, free, and open-source tool for power users and teams who need to organize complex coding agent tasks and maintain a clear, auditable Git-based history of their development process.

name: pi-agent-ide
pricingDetail: Free (No paid plans)
description: Pi Agent IDE is an agent-native extension for the Pi coding agent that provides a unified set of tools for code understanding, editing, debugging, and system observation. It supports both local resources and remote SSH-based environments with features like guarded editing and built-in rollback capabilities.
keyFeatures: Unified interface for reading, searching, and semantic editing
Persistent terminal sessions and interactive debugger support
Guarded snapshot-based editing with automatic rollback
LSP-based code analysis and navigation
Cross-platform file and directory manipulation
bestFor: Developers using the Pi coding agent who require precise, tool-integrated control over code manipulation and debugging within complex projects.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a highly stable, production-ready environment, as the tool is experimental and subject to frequent interface changes.
recentUpdates: Version 0.9.8 was released on 2026-11-08, following significant October 2026 updates (0.9.0-0.9.2) that introduced dedicated search tools like ast_search, lsp_search, and file_search, as well as improvements to VS Code debugger integration and terminal performance.
verdict: A powerful, highly capable experimental toolkit offering superior semantic control for Pi-based AI coding workflows, best suited for early adopters.

name: MiMo Code
pricingDetail: Pay-as-you-go API (billed by usage), Token Plan Individual Lite ($6/month), Standard ($16/month), Pro ($50/month), Max ($100/month), Token Plan Team Standard ($16/seat/month), Pro ($50/seat/month), Max ($100/seat/month)
description: MiMo Code is a terminal-native AI coding assistant designed by Xiaomi to handle long-horizon programming tasks through advanced memory management and autonomous agentic workflows. It supports seamless interaction across terminal, desktop, and IDE environments, enabling developers to map codebases, plan features, and execute complex edits with persistent state.
keyFeatures: Persistent cross-session memory using SQLite FTS5
Three built-in agent modes: build, plan, and compose
Autonomous subagent system and task tracking
Deterministic JavaScript-based workflows
Automatic context reconstruction and budgeting
bestFor: Solo developers and terminal-first engineers who require long-running, multi-turn coding sessions where context persistence across hundreds of interactions is critical.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring SSO, role-based access control (RBAC), audit logs, or enterprises needing formal managed support contracts and SLAs.
recentUpdates: On 2026-08-19, v0.1.13 introduced scoped OpenAI-compatible interfaces for local TUI sessions, enhanced MCP tool invocation, and added the MIMOCODE_CODEX_MODE for unified prompt usage. Previous updates in August 2026 focused on credential isolation, memory writing controls, and multi-session orchestrator improvements.
verdict: A powerful, terminal-centric agentic tool that excels at maintaining context over long-horizon tasks, though it lacks the administrative features required by larger enterprise teams.

name: molt
description: Molt, also branded as Maat Agent, is an open-source coding agent that integrates with terminal and desktop environments to ensure coding tasks are verified against real disk states. It refuses to mark a task as done until project-specific checks defined in a configuration file pass, providing a hash-chained receipt for every attempt.
keyFeatures: Automatic completion checks against real disk state using .molt/done.yml
Hash-chained journals and receipts for every attempt, including refusals
Support for OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Anthropic, and local models
Desktop application for macOS, Windows, and Linux alongside a TUI/CLI
Integrity ledger for tamper-evident tracking of agent actions
bestFor: Developers who require strict validation of coding agent outputs against automated tests, builds, and file-system assertions before accepting them as complete.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a fully managed, hosted agent service that does not require an API key or local model configuration, or projects lacking automated checks to verify progress.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.2 unified the desktop app and CLI under a single engine; the npm package @solvyx/molt was unpublished on 2026-10-07.
verdict: A specialized, strictly-typed open-source tool that prioritizes truth and verification over mere completion, ideal for workflows where false positives are costly.

name: Prime Agent
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month)
description: Prime Agent is an open-source, self-improving coding and research agent designed for long-running, autonomous workflows. It utilizes a Recursive Language Model (RLM) architecture that treats context as variables and subagents as programmatic function calls within a persistent Python REPL.
keyFeatures: Recursive Language Model (RLM) with persistent Python REPL
Continual Harness for self-improving prompts and skill updates via /refine
Daemon-backed sessions for long-running tasks that persist across terminal closures
Direct agent-to-agent communication and orchestration
Native Rust implementation for improved performance and concurrency
bestFor: Research and coding workloads that require long-horizon autonomous operation, persistent memory, and programmatic control over subagent delegation.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a secure sandbox for untrusted code, users who prefer a stable and simple turn-based interaction model, or Windows users looking for a fully production-hardened experience.
recentUpdates: Version 0.10.5 (2026-11-18) updated the harness store path logic, improved skill management, and fixed various installation and discovery issues.
verdict: Prime Agent is a sophisticated research-oriented tool that offers a unique, programmable RLM architecture, though its lack of a true security sandbox and potential for reward-hacking require cautious use in autonomous mode.

name: CodeAF
pricingDetail: CodeAF is free and open-source under the Apache 2.0 license. Users pay their own model providers for token usage or utilize local models at no cost.
description: CodeAF is an open-source terminal-based software factory designed to manage teams of coding agents from a single window. It supports complex workflows by allowing users to hand off tasks that agents execute, check, and merge on individual branches.
keyFeatures: Built-in specialists for coding (/senior-dev), security auditing (/sec), and GitHub pull request reviews (/review)
Pareto crewing that automatically assigns models to specific tasks based on cost-to-quality efficiency
Headless mode for CI, cron, and scripted automation via 'do', 'exec', and 'run' commands
Standing orders that continue executing after the terminal window is closed
Integrated budget controls with per-task and daily spending limits
bestFor: Large, well-specified coding changes, automated security audits, GitHub pull request reviews, and running complex, multi-agent software teams from a single terminal interface.
notIdealFor: Users who prefer a single-agent conversation model or those on Windows who require the full suite of built-in specialists, as these are currently only available on macOS and Linux.
recentUpdates: Version 0.8.3 (2026-11-19) introduced significantly improved patience settings for slow local models and optimized request handling for local endpoints. Earlier updates in October 2026 added AI providers like ai&, specialized security and review commands, and enhanced team management features.
verdict: CodeAF is a highly capable, open-source terminal agent factory that excels at orchestrating complex, multi-step development tasks and providing granular control over model costs and agent workflows.

name: Herdr
description: Herdr is an open-source runtime and native app designed for managing multiple coding agents across local machines and remote servers. It tracks agent states such as working, blocked, or idle, allowing developers to monitor and coordinate multiple autonomous sessions from a single interface.
keyFeatures: Cross-machine agent management via SSH
Real-time state tracking (working, blocked, idle) for coding agents
Background execution server (herdr-core) for session persistence
Agent-native API for task delegation and coordination
Customizable layouts and UI via configuration files
bestFor: Developers who run four or more coding agents simultaneously across multiple repositories and require remote access or session visibility.
notIdealFor: Users who only run one agent at a time, rely on processes that must survive a system reboot, or prefer traditional terminal multiplexers like tmux without the overhead of an agent-focused runtime.
recentUpdates: Version 0.9.5 (2026-10-14) provided hotfixes for input method regressions and addressed session tracking issues for Claude Code and Codex.
verdict: Herdr is a powerful, free runtime for power users managing high-volume agent workflows, though its status as relatively young software with VC backing has prompted some community debate regarding long-term monetization.

name: Agent Deck
description: Agent Deck is a terminal-based session manager designed to provide a unified control layer for managing multiple AI coding agent sessions. It allows developers to monitor, organize, and interact with various CLI agents like Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode from a single interface.
keyFeatures: Unified TUI for monitoring and switching between multiple agent sessions
Cost tracking dashboard with real-time budget limits and usage monitoring
Isolated git worktree management for parallel development tasks
MCP (Model Context Protocol) management and socket pooling to reduce memory usage
Notification bridges for Slack, Telegram, Discord, and Mattermost
bestFor: Developers who frequently run multiple terminal-based AI coding agents simultaneously and need a centralized way to track status, costs, and project context.
notIdealFor: Beginners seeking a managed all-in-one IDE or users who prefer a native graphical interface over a terminal-based workflow.
recentUpdates: Version 1.16.40 (2026-11-22) introduced the Antigravity CLI as a built-in tool, an owner to-do list feature, a recall timeline filter, and added a required --force flag when removing running sessions.
verdict: Agent Deck is a highly effective, practical control layer for power users of terminal AI agents, offering strong session supervision and efficiency tools, though it requires a mature CLI-centric development workflow to be useful.

name: Memdoor
pricingDetail: Pro ($10/month)
description: Memdoor is a terminal-based coding agent and deterministic workflow runner shipped as a single static binary. It enables users to execute repeatable, check-gated coding tasks locally, over SSH, or in CI pipelines using their own model providers or local models.
keyFeatures: Deterministic YAML-based workflows with parallel steps and approval gates
Decision model for token optimization and judged file reading
Multi-provider support including local models via Ollama, vLLM, and llama.cpp
Headless-first CLI designed for CI/CD, scripting, and cron jobs
Team Mode for multi-agent workflows that can outperform single-model coding tasks
bestFor: Developers seeking a scriptable, model-agnostic coding agent that handles complex, repeatable, and verified tasks locally or in CI environments.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a polished GUI-based IDE or managed SaaS platforms with hosted infrastructure and comprehensive enterprise-tier support.
recentUpdates: Released v1.827.0 on November 12, 2026. On October 31, 2026, the team-solve workflow achieved a mean score of 9.8/10 on the LiveCodeBench Hard list.
verdict: A high-performance, open-source CLI agent that excels at deterministic workflow automation and makes small open-weight models highly competitive for coding tasks.

name: agent-mcts
pricingDetail: Free (MIT License). Costs depend on the underlying agent and model usage.
description: agent-mcts is a test-time search harness that wraps coding agent CLIs in a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) engine. It explores multiple solution branches in parallel, evaluates them using tests or an LLM judge, and helps developers select and apply the most successful path.
keyFeatures: Real Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) with UCT selection and backtracking
Isolated execution environments using Git worktrees
Multi-strategy evaluation via test commands, LLM judges, or generated tests
Live terminal tree visualization with support for pausing, resuming, and parallel execution
Agent-agnostic architecture supporting Claude Code, with adapters for others like Codex
bestFor: Developers seeking more reliable code fixes for well-specified tasks where success can be verified by tests or automated judging.
notIdealFor: Quick one-off edits, vague bug reports without test coverage, or tasks where token costs are a primary constraint.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.1 was released on November 22, 2026, following the release of v0.4.0 (generated tests) and v0.3.0 (LLM judge, parallel runs, and resume functionality) earlier that week.
verdict: A specialized, early-stage research tool that effectively brings tree search capabilities to existing coding agents, significantly improving success rates on complex software tasks at the expense of higher token usage.

name: Trix
description: Trix is a terminal workspace and background server built in Rust for running multiple CLI coding agents side by side. It provides real-time state tracking, desktop notifications, and integrated management features to help developers monitor agent activity without manually checking individual panes.
keyFeatures: Per-process agent hooks for state monitoring and notifications
Needs-you strip and desktop alerts for blocked agents
Integrated Git worktree management for parallel agent sessions
Token cost tracking and context window gauges for specific agents
Agent control commands to spawn, send, read, or wait on other agents
bestFor: Developers running multiple CLI coding agents simultaneously who need to quickly identify which tasks require human input or have completed.
notIdealFor: Windows users or individuals who prefer a graphical desktop interface over a terminal-based environment.
recentUpdates: Version 1.5.0 released on November 23, 2026, added agent cloning (alt+t) and shared instruction files. Version 1.4.3 was released on November 22, 2026, focusing on parallel process restoration and scrollback configurations.
verdict: An efficient, agent-first terminal multiplexer that offers deep state observability and cost monitoring, though it is currently in its early, fast-moving release stages.

name: Warp
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Build ($20/month), Max ($200/month), Business ($50/user/month), Enterprise (Custom)
description: Warp is an open-source, AI-native terminal that integrates a modern command-line interface with built-in coding agents, cloud automation, and software factory infrastructure. It allows developers to run interactive commands, manage AI conversations, and automate workflows directly within their development environment.
keyFeatures: Modern terminal with IDE-like editing and command blocks
Warp Agent for multi-step tasks, shell execution, and debugging
Support for third-party CLI agents like Claude Code and Codex
Warp Factories for building automated software workflows
Cloud-based collaboration through shared drives and sessions
bestFor: Terminal-heavy developers who want a unified environment for shell work, built-in AI agents, and side-by-side management of third-party CLI tools.
notIdealFor: Developers who require fixed, predictable monthly costs, teams needing self-hosted agent execution outside of the Enterprise tier, or users with strict requirements against vendor-side data collection.
recentUpdates: In August 2026, Warp rebranded the Oz agent UI to Warp Agent. On August 27, 2026, Warp Factories entered Early Access. On October 7, 2026, Warp added Kiro CLI support to its terminal integrations.
verdict: Warp is a highly capable, terminal-centric platform that effectively bridges local agent usage with cloud-based automation, though users should carefully navigate its usage-based pricing and privacy settings.

name: Wave
description: Wave is an open-source, AI-native terminal that integrates graphical features like file previews, web browsing, and a built-in editor into the command-line experience. It allows developers to manage remote SSH sessions and organize workspaces using a layout of blocks and widgets.
keyFeatures: Durable SSH sessions that persist through network interruptions
Multi-modal AI assistant with support for local models and BYOK
Integrated GUI tools including a VSCode-like editor, web browser, and file previews
WSH CLI for programmatic workspace management and AI interaction
Customizable workspace layouts with support for dashboards and widgets
bestFor: Developers seeking a widget-based, graphical terminal experience with advanced remote file management and AI integration over SSH.
notIdealFor: Users requiring specialized protocol support like serial, Telnet, X11 forwarding, or formal SFTP client management.
recentUpdates: Recent releases include the v0.14.5 update (April 2026) which added a Process Viewer widget and Quake Mode, followed by v0.14.4 (March 2026) which introduced vertical tab bars and upgraded to xterm.js v6.
verdict: A powerful, open-source terminal that bridges the gap between CLI efficiency and graphical productivity, though it lacks some legacy protocol support.

name: TermRover
pricingDetail: Pro ($24.99/year), Pro Lifetime ($79.99/once)
description: TermRover is an AI-native SSH and Mosh terminal for iOS and Android optimized for mobile multiplexer workflows and interacting with coding agents. It provides a tactile, touch-first experience for managing remote tmux, Herdr, Rex, and Zellij sessions.
keyFeatures: Native touch-optimized tmux and multiplexer controls
Mosh support for resilient mobile connectivity
Voice dictation and image-to-agent attachment capabilities
Agents Fleet for tracking and calling coding agents
Built-in SFTP file browser for managing remote files
bestFor: Developers who need to manage remote terminal multiplexers and interact with CLI coding agents while on the go.
notIdealFor: Users seeking an all-in-one local Linux environment, a hosted agent-supervision dashboard, or a desktop-style interface without mobile-specific optimizations.
recentUpdates: Version 1.5.2 (2026-11-21) added customization for upload paths and improved Herdr/Agents Fleet text handling. Version 1.5.0 (2026-11-13) introduced support for Rex multiplexer sessions.
verdict: TermRover is a highly capable, terminal-first tool that excels at making mobile interaction with remote agents and multiplexers feel natural and efficient, offering a robust free tier that covers the most essential professional needs.

name: uniTerm
description: uniTerm is a lightweight, all-in-one terminal emulator that supports over 30 connection protocols, including SSH, RDP, databases, and container management. It features a built-in autonomous AI Agent capable of planning and executing multi-round shell commands directly within the terminal.
keyFeatures: Autonomous AI Agent for multi-turn shell command planning and execution
Support for 30+ protocols (SSH, RDP, VNC, SQL, K8s, Docker, S3, etc.)
Built-in network tools including packet capture and firewall management
Encrypted cross-device configuration sync via Git or WebDAV
Docker-based web deployment for multi-tenant remote access
bestFor: Developers and system administrators who require a unified, feature-dense tool to manage diverse remote infrastructure, databases, and containerized environments.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a strictly mobile-native experience or those who cannot manage external API keys required for the AI agent functionalities.
recentUpdates: Version 1.12.4 (2026-11-21) introduced network traffic capture, remote firewall management, a dockable notes panel, and expanded file browser support for local and WSL systems. Version 1.12.0 (2026-11-09) added Docker web multi-tenant deployment, local services (HTTP, TFTP, SSH, etc.), terminal session recording, and multi-host batch execution.
verdict: A powerful and highly extensible terminal emulator that successfully integrates traditional administrative tasks with modern, AI-driven automation for power users.

name: cmux
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Pro ($50/month), Max ($200/month), Team ($60/user/month)
description: cmux is a native macOS terminal built on libghostty, designed to provide a programmable, multitasking environment for developers managing multiple AI coding agents. It features a sidebar for monitoring agent status, notification rings for alerts, and a scriptable API to orchestrate complex agent-driven workflows.
keyFeatures: Native macOS app with GPU-accelerated rendering via libghostty
Sidebar for tracking agent state, git branches, and notifications
Scriptable CLI and socket API for workspace and browser automation
Persistent Cloud VMs for background agent execution
Cross-device synchronization with an iOS companion app
bestFor: macOS developers who work with multiple AI coding agents simultaneously and need a GUI-based, organized way to monitor session status and agent output.
notIdealFor: Users on Windows or Linux, as cmux is currently an exclusive native macOS application.
recentUpdates: Version 0.65.2 (October 14, 2026) added improvements to agent session restores and cloud infrastructure stability. Version 0.65.0 (October 5, 2026) introduced agent support on SSH hosts, predictive local echo for remote sessions, and a comprehensive settings redesign.
verdict: cmux is a high-performance, developer-focused tool that effectively solves the context-switching fatigue common in agent-driven development by providing deep integration and native visibility into agent workflows.

name: Corgi
description: Corgi is an agent-oriented terminal multiplexer that allows developers to run multiple AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Pi, and OpenCode in side-by-side panes. It tracks the status of each agent, providing visual indicators for when they are working, finished, or require user attention.
keyFeatures: Agent status indicators with F1 quick-jump to active tasks
Persistent sessions that maintain processes after detaching
Integrated Git worktree management
Activity tracking and token usage monitoring per agent
Scriptable CLI for automating terminal sessions and agent control
bestFor: Developers managing multiple AI coding agents in parallel who need to track agent status, token consumption, and workspace activity in a single terminal environment.
notIdealFor: Users who do not work with AI coding agents, those requiring native Windows support, or teams seeking a mature, stable software solution.
recentUpdates: The project launched on October 23, 2026, with ongoing refinements to the CLI, viewer, and interface components.
verdict: Corgi is a promising and ergonomically focused tool for heavy terminal-agent users, though as a very young, experimental project, it should be approached with caution for non-critical workflows.

name: nodeterm
pricingDetail: Pro Monthly ($9.99/month), Pro Yearly ($79.99/year), Pro Lifetime ($299.00)
description: nodeterm is an AI-native terminal manager that organizes terminal sessions and coding agents as interactive nodes on an infinite canvas. It leverages persistent tmux sessions to ensure work survives app restarts or machine reboots while providing a visual workspace for monitoring agent status and managing project tasks.
keyFeatures: Infinite spatial canvas for terminals and agents
Persistent tmux-backed sessions that survive reboots
Kanban board view with live session cards
AI agent monitoring with status badges and subagent transcripts
iOS companion app and web-based Server Edition
bestFor: Developers managing multiple parallel AI agent sessions who prefer a spatial, visual workspace over traditional stacked terminal tabs.
notIdealFor: Users requiring an OSI-approved open-source license, or Windows users who need stable, signed installers and full session continuity today.
recentUpdates: Version 0.5.1 (2026-11-06) introduced chat view improvements including interruptible Claude runs via Esc, plugin/skill completion in the composer, and improved notification behavior for background agents.
verdict: A powerful, innovative workspace for AI-heavy workflows that successfully replaces tabbed terminal fatigue with a cohesive, persistent canvas, though its source-available license and beta-stage Windows support are key considerations.

name: Harp
pricingDetail: Free (Open source under AGPL-3.0)
description: Harp is an unofficial macOS fork of the Warp terminal that replaces the standard tab bar with a specialized sidebar. It is designed to manage multiple Claude Code and Codex agents simultaneously, providing visibility into their working, waiting, or completed states.
keyFeatures: Agent status rows showing working, waiting, and done states
Automatic Claude Code and Codex usage limit rings
Named tab groups with tmux integration for persistence
Bundled Claude Code status plugin with no manual setup required
Self-updating application via GitHub releases
bestFor: macOS developers who use multiple Claude Code or Codex sessions and need a clear, unified view of agent activity and usage limits.
notIdealFor: Users on Linux or Windows, those requiring officially supported Warp builds, or developers seeking integration for agents other than Claude Code and Codex.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.8 (October 29, 2026) added 'needs you' status indicators for Codex sessions and improved task name clarity in the sidebar rows.
verdict: A focused, early-stage, and highly practical fork for power users of Warp who need better agent orchestration, though it remains an unofficial, single-maintainer project.

name: Horus
pricingDetail: Free (Open Source)
description: Horus is an AI-native terminal for Android that provides a full ARM64 Linux workspace (Alpine or Debian) allowing users to run coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode directly on their device. It functions as a standalone development environment that persists in the background, with an optional CLI for USB-based remote access from a laptop.
keyFeatures: Native execution of Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode
Full Linux environment (Alpine or Debian 13) via PRoot
Background process support for long-running agent sessions
USB-based remote access via horus-cli for SSH and file sync
Privacy-focused with no telemetry and optional password locking
bestFor: Developers who want to run CLI coding agents on an Android phone or repurpose spare devices into portable development boxes.
notIdealFor: iPhone users, legacy devices (pre-Android 7.0), 32-bit hardware, or heavy compute tasks requiring desktop-class memory and CPU.
recentUpdates: Version 1.2.2 (Nov 18, 2026) fixed agent install failures and improved error messaging; version 1.2.1 (Nov 12, 2026) addressed install issues on Android 13; version 1.2.0 (Nov 7, 2026) introduced terminal text copying and improved user management.
verdict: A polished, open-source tool that effectively transforms an Android phone into a functional, private Linux development environment for modern AI coding agents.

name: Jules by Google
pricingDetail: Jules (Free), Jules in Pro ($19.99/month), Jules in Ultra ($99.99/month)
description: Jules is an autonomous coding agent designed to handle routine development tasks by cloning repositories into cloud-based virtual machines to execute plans and generate pull requests. It integrates directly with GitHub to manage bug fixes, dependency updates, and maintenance chores asynchronously.
keyFeatures: Autonomous asynchronous task execution in cloud VMs
Automated CI failure detection and resolution via CI Fixer
GitHub integration with PR generation
MCP server support for external tool connections
Proactive task identification and scheduled maintenance
bestFor: Offloading repetitive, non-urgent tasks like dependency version bumps, lint fixes, test scaffolding, and resolving CI failures in GitHub-hosted projects.
notIdealFor: Real-time pair programming, debugging complex state issues, large projects exceeding 50,000 lines, or repositories hosted outside of GitHub.
recentUpdates: On October 29, 2026, Google announced that Jules will be wound down on December 31, 2026, with the service entering read-only mode after November 11, 2026.
verdict: Jules is an effective tool for automating maintenance and backlog tasks, but it is being discontinued at the end of 2026 as Google transitions its agentic development learnings to platforms like Google Antigravity.

name: OpenHands
pricingDetail: Open Source (Free), Teams ($500/month), Enterprise (Custom pricing)
description: OpenHands is an open-source platform for autonomous software engineering agents that can perform tasks like editing files, running tests, and managing pull requests. It provides a developer control center that integrates with existing engineering workflows via local, cloud, or enterprise-hosted backends.
keyFeatures: Autonomous agent task execution within isolated, containerized sandboxes
Support for multiple agent backends including local, remote, and private cloud
Compatibility with any ACP-compatible agent such as Claude Code, Codex, or Gemini
Native integrations for GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Jira, and Linear
Model-agnostic architecture allowing Bring Your Own LLM (BYOK)
bestFor: Developers and teams who require a self-hosted or private-cloud autonomous coding assistant that keeps code and data within their own infrastructure.
notIdealFor: Users who want a simple, zero-maintenance autocomplete tool or those who prefer not to manage infrastructure, sandbox hosts, or individual API model keys.
recentUpdates: Version 1.36.0, released on 2026-11-05, introduced significant enhancements to automations, including new template management, improved repository picking for Data Center providers, and updated service account workflows for agent sessions.
verdict: OpenHands is an industry-leading open-source solution for autonomous coding, offering immense value through its MIT-licensed core, though users must be prepared to manage their own operational overhead or pay for the premium team and enterprise tiers.

name: SWE-agent
company: Princeton University (in collaboration with Stanford University)
pricingDetail: Free (MIT License). Users are responsible for their own LLM API costs and local or cloud compute expenses for Docker environments.
description: SWE-agent is an autonomous software engineering tool that uses a custom Agent-Computer Interface to enable language models to navigate, edit, and execute code within a Docker sandbox to fix GitHub issues. It is primarily designed as a research-oriented framework for studying autonomous agents, benchmarking, and cybersecurity tasks.
keyFeatures: Agent-Computer Interface for interactive file navigation and editing
Massively parallel code execution via SWE-ReX
End-to-end trajectory logging for research analysis
Full Docker sandbox isolation for all tool calls
EnIGMA mode for offensive cybersecurity and CTF challenges
bestFor: Researchers and academics studying autonomous program repair, agent-computer interfaces, or those reproducing SWE-bench results and security researchers using the EnIGMA mode.
notIdealFor: Beginners seeking a GUI or IDE plugin, teams requiring vendor support, or developers needing a production-grade automated pull-request bot, as the project has been superseded for general use.
recentUpdates: The project is in maintenance-only mode following the v1.1.0 release on May 2025, which added support for SWE-smith and multilingual evaluation. The maintainers now explicitly recommend mini-swe-agent for new work.
verdict: While historically significant for its contribution to Agent-Computer Interface research and benchmarking, SWE-agent has been superseded by mini-swe-agent. It remains a valuable, well-instrumented tool for ML research and specific cybersecurity use cases, but it is not intended for standard software development workflows.

name: mini-swe-agent
description: mini-swe-agent is a minimal, MIT-licensed AI software engineering agent designed for research, benchmarking, and hackable workflows. It operates by providing language models with a simple bash-only interface and a linear execution history, enabling transparency and compatibility with any model via LiteLLM.
keyFeatures: Minimal core agent class (approx. 100 lines of Python code)
Bash-only tool interface with no requirement for native tool-calling
Linear message history ideal for debugging and fine-tuning
Environment support including Docker, Podman, Singularity, and local execution
Universal model compatibility via LiteLLM, OpenRouter, and Portkey
bestFor: Researchers and tinkerers needing a transparent, hackable baseline for benchmarking models, fine-tuning, or running sandboxed batch evaluations.
notIdealFor: Developers seeking an out-of-the-box product with IDE integration, graphical approval interfaces, or managed team support.
recentUpdates: The project is currently on v2 (version 2.4.6 released 2026-07-23), which introduced native tool calling as the default, support for multimodal input, and a new structure for trajectories.
verdict: A radically simple, transparent, and model-agnostic coding agent that serves as an excellent research baseline, though it lacks the polish and features of full-scale IDE-integrated coding assistants.

name: Sweep
pricingDetail: Basic ($10/month), Pro ($20/month), Ultra ($60/month)
description: Sweep is an AI-powered coding assistant built specifically for the JetBrains IDE ecosystem. It features a custom, fine-tuned next-edit autocomplete model and an autonomous agent capable of performing codebase-wide tasks, bug fixes, and inline code modifications.
keyFeatures: Next-edit autocomplete with custom Tab model
Autonomous agent for multi-file code generation and editing
Context-aware codebase indexing
Privacy Mode with zero data retention
Remote MCP server support with OAuth 2.0/2.1
bestFor: Individual developers and teams working primarily in JetBrains IDEs who need a native-feeling assistant for routine coding tasks and bug fixes.
notIdealFor: Mixed-editor teams using VS Code or other IDEs and users requiring high-level architectural reasoning for complex systems engineering.
recentUpdates: As of January 2026, updates included background bash tool execution, improved UI for thinking blocks, and enhanced agent autocomplete. Note: Reports from October 2026 indicate the service has become unavailable.
verdict: Sweep is a highly capable, JetBrains-native coding assistant that excels at routine in-IDE tasks, though its recent market availability has become uncertain as of late 2026.

name: Ellipsis
pricingDetail: Standard ($5,000/month), Advanced ($10,000/month), Premier ($15,000/month)
description: Ellipsis is a cloud-based platform for managing and governing agentic workflows by providing secure sandboxes for various coding agents. It allows teams to define, deploy, and monitor agents via YAML configurations, supporting triggers from sources like GitHub, Slack, Linear, and Sentry.
keyFeatures: Harness-agnostic platform supporting agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini
Managed secure sandboxes with defined permissions and spend caps
Observability into every tool call, session log, and thinking token
Versioned agent configurations defined as YAML files
Deployment options in Ellipsis managed cloud or your own AWS VPC
bestFor: Engineering teams that need to run and govern multiple coding agents in background workflows, code review pipelines, or software factories with strict budget and permission controls.
notIdealFor: Teams seeking an install-and-forget, zero-configuration AI code review bot, as the platform now requires defining and maintaining agent YAML configurations.
recentUpdates: Launched the Ellipsis Agent Cloud on July 28, 2026, pivoting the company from a dedicated code review bot to a comprehensive agent infrastructure and governance platform.
verdict: Ellipsis is a highly practical, governance-focused infrastructure tool for teams scaling their use of autonomous coding agents, offering necessary safety controls that simple agent harnesses lack.

name: Cosine
pricingDetail: Starter ($19/month), Builder ($49/month), Team ($99/month), Scale ($199/month), Professional ($999/month), Enterprise (Custom)
description: Genie is an autonomous AI software engineering agent designed to handle background tasks like refactoring, migrations, and bug fixes without needing real-time supervision. It operates by retrieving codebase context, planning solutions, and generating validated pull requests, often running asynchronously to allow engineers to focus on other work.
keyFeatures: Autonomous agent loop for planning, writing, and testing code
Parallel agent orchestration for complex, large-scale migrations
Deployment flexibility including public cloud, VPC, and air-gapped environments
Support for legacy languages like COBOL, Fortran, and Verilog
Integration with development workflows via CLI, Desktop, and Cloud platform
bestFor: Engineering teams maintaining long-lived, complex, or legacy codebases in regulated industries like defense, government, and finance where security and data sovereignty are critical.
notIdealFor: Teams focused primarily on greenfield JavaScript or TypeScript development, or organizations that require a general-purpose AI assistant for chat-based research and writing rather than autonomous engineering tasks.
recentUpdates: The company has rebranded its model family to Lumen, including the Scout and Outpost models, while shifting its long-term focus toward sovereign AI with the upcoming Lumen Sovereign model family scheduled for Q1 2027.
verdict: Genie is a highly capable, autonomous engineering tool that excels in high-security environments and legacy codebases, though its credit-based pricing and specialized focus make it less suited for casual or general-purpose development teams.

name: OpenYak
pricingDetail: Free (Free), Premium models (metered, via OpenRouter or personal API keys), ChatGPT subscription (direct)
description: OpenYak is a local-first desktop AI agent designed to operate within your local file system, native desktop applications, and web browsers. It provides a graphical interface that allows users to monitor task progress, manage workspaces, and maintain data privacy by keeping conversations and memory on the local machine.
keyFeatures: Native Computer and Browser workspaces with shared human-agent control
Local-first architecture that stores files and memory on your machine
Support for 20+ model providers and local models via Ollama or Rapid-MLX
46+ pre-configured MCP connectors for integrations
Built-in channel runtime for messaging platforms like Slack, Discord, and Telegram
bestFor: Local-first teams and power users who need to automate complex workflows across local files, desktop applications, and web browsers while maintaining data privacy and auditability.
notIdealFor: Users looking for a hosted web chatbot skin or those requiring cloud-managed, multi-device synchronization for sensitive AI workspace contexts.
recentUpdates: Version 1.5.0-rc.3 introduced pinned side-by-side computer and browser workspaces, while version 1.5.0-rc.2 added native Computer Use and a managed Browser workspace with shared control capabilities.
verdict: OpenYak is a highly capable, privacy-focused alternative to platform-locked AI agents, offering significant transparency and control for desktop-based automation tasks.

name: DeepAgents JS
pricingDetail: Free (MIT License); users pay only for the LLM model providers and any infrastructure used.
description: DeepAgents JS is an opinionated, ready-to-run agent harness that provides a pre-assembled toolkit for autonomous agents. It streamlines complex workflows by including built-in features for planning, virtual filesystem management, sub-agent delegation, and context handling without requiring manual integration of these components.
keyFeatures: Built-in task planning via write_todos
Virtual filesystem for memory and context (ls, read_file, edit_file)
Isolated sub-agent delegation for parallel tasks
Native LangGraph support with streaming and persistence
Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for external tools
bestFor: Autonomous agents handling complex, long-running, and multi-step tasks like research or coding projects.
notIdealFor: Simple, single-step tasks or scenarios where the overhead of an agent harness is unnecessary.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.2 released on 2026-11-24 introduced on-demand MCP tool discovery, message support for local sessions (Claude Code/dcode), and support for confidential OAuth clients.
verdict: A robust, batteries-included framework for developers who need to quickly deploy sophisticated, reliable autonomous agents on top of the LangChain and LangGraph ecosystem.

name: Orkas
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Lite (Custom pricing), Pro (Custom pricing), Max (Custom pricing), Enterprise (Custom pricing)
description: Orkas is an open-source, local-first multi-agent desktop application that acts as a coordinated AI workforce for macOS and Windows. A central Commander agent manages project-based workflows, delegating tasks to various specialist agents to automate complex processes like research, content creation, and e-commerce operations.
keyFeatures: Autonomous Commander agent for multi-step workflow coordination
Local-first architecture with private, on-device data storage
Scheduled automations and auto-advance for continuous background task execution
Support for built-in specialist agents and external CLI tools like Claude Code and Codex
Project-based context management for memory and collaborative work
bestFor: Professionals and small teams needing an ongoing, project-based AI team to handle complex, multi-step business processes and recurring automated tasks.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a simple, general-purpose chatbot for one-off queries or developers looking for a pure code library to integrate into external applications.
recentUpdates: The v2026.11.16 release introduced improvements to content workbench, media services, and video timeline management, while v2026.11.4 added support for GPT-6.1 Terra and refined automation scheduling.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-focused desktop client that elevates AI from a simple chat tool into a persistent, autonomous project team ideal for managing long-term business operations.

name: Kody
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Pro ($12/month or $120/year)
description: Kody acts as an autonomous and asynchronous agents' cloud that provides AI models with durable state, secure credential storage, and a cloud-based execution environment. It enables agents to maintain memory across sessions, run tasks while offline, and interact with secure integrations without needing direct access to sensitive credentials.
keyFeatures: Durable memory and credential storage
Scheduled jobs, workflows, and webhooks
Package-based reusable code with typed inputs
Agent-first file workspace management
Cross-agent identity profiles
bestFor: Developers and power users of AI agents who need to add persistence, scheduled automation, and secure API handling to their existing agent workflows.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a standalone chat interface or those who do not wish to manage or connect infrastructure, as Kody is not an AI model or chat client.
recentUpdates: The v2026.11.24 release added referral support for organizations and performance improvements. Earlier, in November 2026, Kody introduced workspace file management, agent identity profiles, and native desktop app support as experimental features.
verdict: Kody is a robust infrastructure layer that effectively bridges the gap between ephemeral agent conversations and permanent, reliable software automations.

name: Omnigent
pricingDetail: Free (Apache 2.0). Users pay only for model usage (Anthropic, OpenAI, or other gateways) and any third-party cloud sandbox providers (such as Modal, E2B, or AWS Lambda) used.
description: Omnigent is an open-source meta-harness that provides a unified orchestration layer for running and supervising multiple AI agents like Claude Code, Codex, and custom YAML-defined agents. It enables real-time collaboration, stateful policy enforcement, and secure sandboxing across terminal, web, and mobile environments.
keyFeatures: Multi-agent orchestration and delegation
Stateful governance policies including spend caps and tool access limits
Secure local and remote cloud sandboxing
Shared live agent sessions for team collaboration
Trigger-based automations for Jira, Slack, GitHub, Linear, and PagerDuty
bestFor: Platform and development teams running two or more coding agents who require centralized policy, spend auditing, and collaborative review workflows.
notIdealFor: Non-technical users, single-agent setups where standard CLI tools are sufficient, and workflows that require a fully managed service with no infrastructure to host or maintain.
recentUpdates: v0.23.0 (2026-11-19) introduced session grids for side-by-side chat monitoring, refined automation controls for MCP services, and added /rewind for Claude SDK and Claude Code. v0.22.0 (2026-11-13) added automated triggers for events like GitHub or Slack and enhanced pull request review tools.
verdict: A robust, open-source orchestration layer that excels at bringing governance and collaborative visibility to complex, multi-agent coding environments, though it requires significant self-hosting and configuration effort.

name: Manus
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Pro ($20/month), Pro ($40/month), Team ($20/seat/month)
description: Manus is an autonomous AI agent that operates within a virtual sandbox environment to plan, execute, and deliver complete work products. It functions as a virtual colleague that manages tasks independently using its own file system and internet-enabled computer.
keyFeatures: Autonomous task execution in a cloud sandbox
Manus Studio for local file and tool integration
Multi-agent team coordination via Cue
Scheduled and triggered workflow automations
Built-in video editing and game development tools
bestFor: Market research, competitive analysis, data-heavy reporting, and rapid prototyping of websites or web apps.
notIdealFor: Tasks requiring guaranteed 100% accuracy, high-stakes financial operations, or complex workflows where an audit trail of model logic is mandatory.
recentUpdates: Launched Manus 2.0 on October 1, 2026, introducing the Cascade internal engine, Manus Studio workspace, advanced Video Editor and Game Dev add-ons, and Remote Control via voice commands.
verdict: Manus is a powerful, innovative autonomous agent for accelerating complex workflows, though it requires human oversight to verify outputs against potential hallucinations or drift in long-running tasks.

name: LoopTroop
description: LoopTroop is a local GUI orchestrator designed for long-running, high-correctness AI software development that manages the lifecycle from idea to merged code. It utilizes a multi-model LLM council for planning, isolated git worktrees for execution, and formal approval gates to ensure accuracy and prevent context drift.
keyFeatures: Multi-model LLM Council for anonymous planning and voting
Isolated execution beads using Git worktrees
Ralph-style recovery loops for automated error handling
Precise context engineering to prevent AI drift
Built-in AI chat assistant with project-wide context awareness
bestFor: Complex, mid-size to large feature work requiring high correctness and reliable, long-running unattended execution.
notIdealFor: Quick one-shot edits, trivial fixes, or chat-first exploratory coding where planning overhead introduces unnecessary latency.
recentUpdates: Version 0.6.4 improved responsiveness, startup speed, and logging performance; version 0.6.3 refined error handling and safety scans; version 0.6.2 introduced an integrated AI chat assistant and improved retry logic.
verdict: LoopTroop is a sophisticated, state-machine-based orchestrator ideal for developers who prioritize accuracy and transparent automation over speed, though it requires a secure sandboxed environment to manage its autonomous execution risks.

name: Muse
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Power ($20/month), Maximum ($100/month)
description: Muse is a personal AI agent from Meta that executes tasks across apps and services by operating within a secure, isolated virtual machine. It is designed to act on user goals, manage background projects, and produce various artifacts, including documents and media, while maintaining human oversight.
keyFeatures: Persistent, isolated Secure Virtual Machine for task execution
Multi-step, background autonomous agentic workflows
Human-in-the-loop approvals for sensitive actions
Artifact generation including documents, PDFs, and dashboards
Cross-platform integration with apps like WhatsApp, Shopify, and QuickBooks
bestFor: Individuals and small businesses seeking to automate administrative tasks, content creation, and goal tracking through existing platforms like Instagram and Facebook.
notIdealFor: Regulated industries handling sensitive health or financial data, or organizations requiring enterprise-level admin controls and audit logs.
recentUpdates: On November 5, 2026, voice conversations and expressive avatars began rolling out. On November 6, 2026, the company introduced Spaces for custom in-app experiences and updated models trained via Muse Wonder.
verdict: A powerful, innovative agentic tool that is strong for individual productivity and marketing workflows, though it remains in a trial phase due to evolving privacy settings and a current lack of centralized business management controls.

name: OtoDock
pricingDetail: Community (Free), Pro (€25/month), Team (€69/month), Business (€199/month)
description: OtoDock is a self-hosted platform designed for managing autonomous AI agent teams on your own infrastructure. It enables collaborative, multi-agent workflows that can be integrated with your existing Claude or OpenAI subscriptions and local models.
keyFeatures: Kernel-level sandboxing and network isolation for every agent
Multi-agent orchestration with departments, delegation, and shared knowledge libraries
Scheduled and triggered automation with webhook integration
Remote machine control allowing agents to execute tasks on local hardware
Direct phone and media capabilities, including video and document generation
bestFor: Privacy-conscious small teams and technical organizations requiring a self-hosted, secure environment for autonomous agents.
notIdealFor: Teams requiring a managed, zero-maintenance SaaS solution or users without the technical expertise to manage a Docker-based server stack.
recentUpdates: Version 1.9.1 (2026-11-04) introduced memory limit management, delegated task execution on local computers, updated AI engine support for GPT-6.1 and Qwen 3.8, and enhanced permissions for scheduled and delegated tasks.
verdict: An ambitious, security-focused agentic OS that offers impressive granular control and transparent licensing, though its broad scope of features requires significant self-hosting investment.

name: Firstmate
description: firstmate is an agent distro that serves as a command layer to coordinate multiple autonomous coding agents across parallel tasks. It allows a user to act as a captain who delegates work to a crew of agents operating in isolated git worktrees and session backends.
keyFeatures: Unified liaison for multiple agent sessions
Event-driven, zero-token supervision
Disposable git worktrees for isolated parallel task execution
Support for persistent secondary agents
Durable, restart-proof state management
bestFor: Developers who need to manage multiple complex, parallel coding tasks or project audits without manual session juggling.
notIdealFor: Users seeking a simple one-click GUI application, model-agnostic tools, Windows users, or those who do not use verified terminal-based coding harnesses.
recentUpdates: On 2026-10-23, the project announced full support for the Rex runtime backend.
verdict: A robust, highly disciplined orchestration layer that transforms general-purpose coding agents into a coordinated, supervised crew, ideal for power users who prioritize structural isolation and automated project management.

name: OpenResearch
pricingDetail: Managed compute (prepaid, at-cost, no markup)
description: OpenResearch is an open-source research agent harness that converts standard coding agents into autonomous research tools. It allows agents to review literature, develop scientific hypotheses, and execute experiments while keeping all research artifacts and data local to the user's machine.
keyFeatures: Native integration with agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode
Literature discovery across alphaXiv, OpenAlex, bioRxiv, and PubMed
Local experiment engine with Git-based versioning and run tracking
Multi-backend compute support (Local, SSH, Slurm, Kubernetes, Modal, Hugging Face)
Local-first data storage for projects, logs, and artifacts
bestFor: Researchers and developers aiming to automate machine learning experimentation and literature reviews using local-first workflows.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a centralized, cloud-hosted research platform or those whose primary needs are unrelated to machine learning experimentation and development.
recentUpdates: Introduced the OpenResearch Intelligence Index on 2026-11-20 to track autoresearch capabilities, following the v0.2.18 release on 2026-10-09 which included various CLI and sandbox execution improvements.
verdict: A powerful, privacy-conscious harness for research-oriented AI agents that successfully bridges the gap between coding tools and scientific experimentation.

name: Coder
pricingDetail: Community (Free), Premium (Contact for quote), AI Premium (Contact for quote)
description: Coder is a self-hosted platform that provides governed cloud development environments and native AI coding agents. It allows organizations to orchestrate AI workflows and workspace provisioning entirely within their own infrastructure to maintain strict security, auditability, and control.
keyFeatures: Native AI agent control plane for self-hosted execution
Headless agent orchestration via API
Environment-as-Code using Terraform
Centralized AI governance, observability, and audit logging
Air-gap capable infrastructure support
bestFor: Regulated industries and enterprises requiring air-gapped or self-hosted environments that demand strict data residency, security, and centralized policy control over AI coding agents.
notIdealFor: Small teams without dedicated infrastructure personnel, or organizations seeking a SaaS-managed developer environment product.
recentUpdates: In September 2026, Coder Agents reached general availability (v2.37), introducing production-ready headless agent APIs, improved model access controls, and integration with Coder’s AI Gateway.
verdict: A robust, enterprise-grade platform for organizations that prioritize infrastructure control and security when deploying AI agents and cloud workspaces.

name: AX (Agent Executor)
pricingDetail: Free (Apache License 2.0). Users are responsible for underlying Kubernetes infrastructure, storage, and model API costs.
description: AX is an open-source, declarative orchestrator designed to run and manage autonomous AI agent workloads at scale within Kubernetes clusters. It utilizes Agent Substrate as a compute runtime to provide isolated sandboxes, stateful task suspension, and workspace management for agentic tasks.
keyFeatures: Isolated sandboxed execution with resource and network limits
Declarative Kubernetes-style API for Task, Workspace, and Model definitions
Suspend and resume capabilities for efficient compute resource management
Interactive debugging tools like ax ssh and task monitoring
High-volume scalability backed by Redis-based state management
bestFor: Platform teams and researchers managing large-scale, bursty, or long-running fleets of agents that require infrastructure-level governance and cost controls.
notIdealFor: Small teams, individual developers, or production environments requiring immediate reliability, as the project is in early development with significant operational overhead and known security gaps.
recentUpdates: Version v0.4.0-rc.1 was released on 2026-11-20, introducing architectural refinements, Postgres integration, and improved handling of actor states and task lifecycles.
verdict: AX offers a powerful and credible architecture for fleet-scale agent orchestration, but it remains an early-stage project that demands heavy operational investment, currently lacking production-grade authentication and mature health monitoring.

name: Agent Substrate
pricingDetail: The software is open-source and free to use; infrastructure costs (GKE, Compute Engine, Cloud Storage) apply.
description: Agent Substrate is a high-density, secure-by-default execution runtime that decouples stateful agent workloads from compute workers to efficiently manage millions of sandboxes. It allows idle agents to be snapshotted to storage and resumed in under 500ms, optimizing resource usage for autonomous, stateful agent applications.
keyFeatures: Stateful actor snapshotting and restoration
Zero-trust, VM-grade isolation via gVisor or microVMs
Per-agent cryptographic identity (SPIFFE/JWT)
Built-in egress gateway for secret injection and access control
High-density execution allowing 10x more agents than standard containers
bestFor: Large-scale platforms running thousands or millions of stateful, mostly-idle agents such as coding assistants, long-term productivity assistants, and reinforcement learning research environments.
notIdealFor: Small teams that can manage agents using simpler, always-on sandbox solutions, or workloads requiring persistent live connections like open database sessions that do not survive agent suspension.
recentUpdates: On 2026-11-05, Agent Substrate reached 1.0, became generally available on GKE, and was accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Recent improvements include request parking in the router to manage oversubscribed pools and support for per-container memory limits in microVMs.
verdict: An essential open-source infrastructure project for organizations needing to scale stateful AI agents on Kubernetes, though it requires significant operational maturity to manage its specific lifecycle and security requirements.

name: Rivet
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Hobby ($18/month), Team ($156/month), Enterprise ($740/month)
description: Rivet is a platform for running and scaling autonomous, durable agents using an actor model that provides in-memory state, persistent SQLite databases, and low-latency execution. It is designed to be highly efficient, allowing thousands of lightweight actors to run on existing infrastructure by offloading state to S3 via its WarpDrive storage engine.
keyFeatures: Durable Actors with persistent SQLite state
High-density execution with 72 KB per actor
Sub-5ms cold starts
Multi-cloud and self-hosted support via a single stateless binary
Integrated cron, scheduling, and WebSocket networking
bestFor: Developers building long-lived, durable AI agents, multiplayer sessions, or workflows that require state persistence across restarts and low-latency communication.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring highly specific, pre-built repository chores like GitHub Agentic Workflows or teams that require a long-standing, independent track record before adoption.
recentUpdates: Rivet 3.0 was released in November 2026, introducing the WarpDrive storage engine for S3-backed SQLite performance. November 2026 updates also included Actor forking for SQLite, general availability of the Rust SDK, and integration support for Alchemy.
verdict: A high-performance, developer-focused infrastructure tool that excels at managing stateful, agentic workloads at scale, though it is a relatively new platform with some features currently in preview.

name: GitHub Agentic Workflows
pricingDetail: GitHub Agentic Workflows (free), GitHub Copilot (requires plan), Third-party AI models (billed by provider).
description: GitHub Agentic Workflows allows developers to automate repository tasks by defining AI-powered agents in Markdown files. These agents are compiled into GitHub Actions and use natural language to perform reasoning-based work like issue triage, code review, and documentation updates.
keyFeatures: Markdown-based workflow definition
Multi-engine support including GitHub Copilot, Claude, Gemini, and OpenAI
Built-in security with sandboxed execution and threat detection
Safe outputs for validated write operations
Native GitHub Actions integration and CI/CD compatibility
bestFor: Tasks requiring reasoning, interpretation, or context, such as issue triage, PR review suggestions, repository reporting, and documentation maintenance.
notIdealFor: Deterministic CI/CD tasks like standard builds, linting, testing, and deployments where procedural scripts are more reliable and cost-effective.
recentUpdates: General availability announced on October 28, 2026, featuring support for Actions Runner Controller (ARC) with Docker-in-Docker, improved budget forecasting, model routing, and enhanced agent isolation via micro-VMs.
verdict: A powerful, secure framework for adding AI reasoning to repository automation, provided it is treated as a supplement to, rather than a replacement for, existing deterministic CI/CD pipelines.

name: Strands Harness SDK
pricingDetail: Free (Apache License 2.0)
description: Strands Agents is an open-source SDK and agent harness for building production-grade AI agents in Python and TypeScript. It provides a complete agent loop with lifecycle controls, memory, and multi-agent patterns, allowing developers to build custom harnesses or use a pre-assembled, benchmarked version called Strands harness.
keyFeatures: Model agnostic with support for Amazon Bedrock, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and local models
Pre-assembled Strands harness with tuned system prompts and built-in context management
Multi-agent orchestration including Graph, Swarm, and agent-to-agent patterns
Production lifecycle controls such as turn limits, token budgets, and human-in-the-loop interventions
Built-in support for MCP, streaming, structured output, and long-term memory
bestFor: Engineering teams building production AI agents who require fine-grained control over the agent loop, observability, and cost-efficient execution.
notIdealFor: Developers requiring extensive community-driven third-party plugins, platforms heavily locked into GCP or Azure, or those needing strictly deterministic, fixed-step pipeline workflows.
recentUpdates: On October 30, 2026, version 1.23.0 was released for the TypeScript SDK, introducing subagent persist interrupts, model information capabilities, and new S3 storage strategies. On November 4, 2026, the project expanded built-in tools (file, web, multi-agent) and deprecated the legacy strands-agents-tools package.
verdict: Strands Agents is a robust, production-ready framework that strikes a strong balance between 'out-of-the-box' usability via Strands harness and deep customizability through its core SDK.

name: Paperclip
pricingDetail: Self-hosted (free under MIT license), Hosted Cloud (€10/month or €100/year)
description: Paperclip is an open-source control plane designed to orchestrate and govern teams of AI agents by providing an organizational structure. It allows users to manage multiple agents from different runtimes through a centralized org chart, task manager, and budget-governance system.
keyFeatures: Org chart with roles, reporting lines, and task ownership
Company, agent, and project-level hard-stop budgets
Approval and review gates for agent tasks and strategic changes
Cross-provider agent support for any runtime that accepts heartbeats
Skill studio and repeatable routines for standardized agent workflows
bestFor: Teams running multiple AI agents in parallel that need a centralized dashboard to track costs, delegate work, and audit agent performance through human-in-the-loop governance.
notIdealFor: Users running only a single agent, those seeking a dedicated AI model or agent-building framework, or teams requiring built-in push notification webhooks.
recentUpdates: The project uses calendar-versioned releases with stable updates occurring regularly, such as the v2026.831.1 stable release in September 2026.
verdict: Paperclip is an effective, highly transparent control plane that treats AI agents like human employees, making it the most robust option for governing agent fleets through real financial and operational constraints.

name: OpenSRE
description: OpenSRE is an autonomous, open-source AI agent designed to investigate and resolve production incidents and CI/CD failures. It connects to infrastructure and observability stacks to provide evidence-based root cause analysis and automated remediation suggestions.
keyFeatures: Autonomous CI/CD reliability analysis and automated pull request fixes
Integration with over 60 observability, cloud, and incident management tools
Model Context Protocol (MCP) support for extensible tool bridging
Interactive terminal-based shell for natural language incident investigation
Configurable deployment options including self-hosted and managed cloud gateways
