Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for agent-assisted history retrieval
Context-rich search including directory, exit code, and duration
Local-first SQLite storage with optional self-hosted synchronization
bestFor: Software engineers, DevOps, and power users who work across multiple machines and frequently utilize AI coding agents.
notIdealFor: Occasional terminal users, users on systems with specific constraints like network filesystems (NFS) or ZFS configurations where SQLite may face performance issues, and those who prefer standard, non-enhanced shell history.
recentUpdates: Version 18.25.1 was released on 2026-11-20. On 2026-10-27, the team introduced Atuin Threads for cross-machine AI session management. Previous updates in 2026 added 32x faster sync via packfiles and open-sourced the Atuin AI server.
verdict: Atuin is a highly effective, free, and open-source solution for terminal power users, offering significant productivity gains through deep search and AI agent integration, though it introduces minor setup and key-management overhead.

name: Modern Web Guidance
description: Modern Web Guidance is a collection of expert-vetted skills designed to provide AI coding agents with accurate web platform expertise and best practices. It helps agents modernize legacy codebases, improve performance, and ensure accessibility by integrating directly into development workflows.
keyFeatures: Expert-vetted web development guides for AI agents
Automated legacy code modernization and scanning
Cross-browser Baseline compatibility data integration
Public evaluation dashboard for agent performance
CLI tool for seamless agent workflow integration
bestFor: Developers using AI coding agents who want to ensure their generated code is accessible, secure, performant, and aligned with modern web standards.
notIdealFor: Developers not using AI-assisted coding agents or those requiring tools outside of standard web platform development.
recentUpdates: Version 1.0.0 released on November 10, 2026, featuring 203 use-case guides, a new codebase modernization scanner, and official stewardship by the Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams.
verdict: An essential utility for modernizing AI-assisted web development workflows by bridging the gap between frontier model outputs and verified, browser-standard web practices.

name: klad
pricingDetail: Personal ($29 once), Early bird ($15 once), Company seat ($79 per seat/year)
description: Klad is a source-available 2D painting and animation application designed to be used in collaboration with coding agents. It provides a full CLI, allowing agents to paint and manipulate artwork directly while maintaining every stroke as editable data rather than static pixels.
keyFeatures: Agent-driven command line interface for painting and editing
Full animation suite with bones, IK, and in-betweening
Pixel art tools with real-time palette management
Direct export to Godot engine
Editable stroke data stored as version-controlled file folders
bestFor: Indie game artists and illustrators working with AI coding agents who need non-destructive, stroke-level control over their artwork.
notIdealFor: Large teams requiring open-source licenses or designers who rely solely on Windows/Linux environments where current support is less mature than macOS.
recentUpdates: Version 0.4.0 (2026-11-19) added an Export menu, right-click menu, color sliders, zoom keys, and klad apply --steps for automated drawing visualization. Version 0.3.0 (2026-11-16) introduced light maps for 2D lighting. Version 0.2.0 (2026-11-12) debuted dedicated pixel art layers.
verdict: A unique, workflow-focused tool that bridges the gap between generative AI and professional art software by keeping all work as editable, git-friendly data.

name: Elephant-Goldfish Model
description: The Elephant-Goldfish Model (EGM) is an open-source plugin designed to improve AI-assisted software development by separating design context from objective validation. It utilizes a long-horizon 'Elephant' agent to maintain project memory and drafting, while 'Goldfish' agents act as stateless, independent reviewers to identify gaps and assumptions.
keyFeatures: Brainstorming and specification drafting with contextual memory
Adversarial validation via stateless review agents
Automated drift reporting between code and documentation
Customizable review loops with flexible standards
Multi-stage review workflows for software design
bestFor: Software engineers and project managers needing to conduct structured design reviews and ensure architectural alignment before implementation.
notIdealFor: Simple coding tasks, routine bug fixes, or environments where the AI host cannot spawn isolated subagents.
recentUpdates: The project released its first tagged version, v0.1.0, on 2026-10-27, following the public open-source announcement on 2026-10-22.
verdict: EGM provides a robust framework for reducing 'AI slop' by enforcing human-in-the-loop design reviews, though it requires a significant token investment and specific agent capabilities to function.

name: opencodex
pricingDetail: Free (No paid plans)
description: Opencodex is a local proxy that serves as a universal gateway, allowing developers to use various LLMs with AI coding tools like Codex, Claude Code, and Claude Desktop. It functions by translating API requests between tools and providers without requiring any modifications to the coding tools themselves.
keyFeatures: Supports 40+ model providers including Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and Ollama
Translates requests for Codex, Claude Code, and other coding agents
Provides a web dashboard for model routing, provider management, and OAuth handling
Enables advanced routing like failover, weighted round-robin, and ChatGPT account pooling

bestFor: Developers who want to use their preferred LLMs with established AI coding tools like Codex or Claude Code, or those looking to manage multiple API keys and provider models in one local interface.
notIdealFor: Users who are uncomfortable configuring model API keys or who prefer an all-in-one software solution that does not require managing a local proxy gateway.

name: Traces
pricingDetail: Core (Free), Custom (Get in touch)
description: Traces is a developer productivity tool that captures, normalizes, and stores AI coding agent sessions into a shared, searchable format. It enables teams to collaborate on agent workflows, maintain historical context, and link coding sessions directly to Git commits.
keyFeatures: Unified cross-agent session history for 16+ ecosystems
Git integration to link commits with session context
Interactive Surfaces for visualizing token usage, security, and file changes
Traces MCP server for agent-based lookups and search
Granular privacy controls including PII redaction and visibility settings

notIdealFor: Teams requiring fully self-hosted storage solutions or those looking to create new organizational accounts immediately, as new org creation is currently paused.

name: AgentMon Live
pricingDetail: Free (Open source under Apache 2.0 license).
description: AgentMon Live is an open-source monitoring tool that provides centralized, local-only visibility into AI coding agent sessions. It tracks tool calls, subagents, file changes, and resource usage across platforms including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and AWS Kiro.
keyFeatures: Unified web-based dashboard for multiple AI agent sessions
Done gate to verify task completion and catch failed tests
Live visualization of subagent activity and tool call flows
Resource usage tracking for tokens, cost, and quota limits
Local-only data privacy with no cloud-based account required
bestFor: Developers managing multiple concurrent sessions in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or AWS Kiro who need unified visibility and verification of agent tasks.
notIdealFor: Users of AI agents other than Claude Code, Codex, and Kiro, or teams requiring centralized, multi-user, or cloud-hosted monitoring platforms.
recentUpdates: Version 0.59.0 (released Nov 19, 2026) added feedback functionality and improved Codex integration. Version 0.57.1 (Nov 18, 2026) introduced custom web views for data visualization. Support for OpenAI Codex and AWS Kiro was added on Nov 17, 2026.
verdict: A highly effective, privacy-focused tool that brings necessary transparency to AI coding workflows, with its done gate being a standout feature for ensuring code quality in autonomous tasks.

name: agentmash
pricingDetail: Free ($0/month), Team ($20/developer/month, or $16/developer/month billed annually), Enterprise (from $15,000/year)
description: Agentmash is a coordination layer for AI coding agents that allows multiple agents to share a repository by reporting edits and warnings across a team. It integrates with tools like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot to prevent agents from overwriting each other's work by injecting conflict advisories directly into the agent's context window.
keyFeatures: Real-time collision warnings for overlapping file edits
Agent task claiming to prevent work duplication
Centralized dashboard for monitoring team-wide agent activity
Live view of repository history and active agent sessions
Strict mode to block conflicting edits until acknowledged
bestFor: Software teams of two or more developers who use multiple AI coding agents on the same repository and frequently encounter merge conflicts.
notIdealFor: Solo developers, or organizations with strict security requirements that prohibit routing file paths and repository activity through external servers (unless using the enterprise self-hosted option).
recentUpdates: Introduced a guided tour by Mash for new users (October 25, 2026), persistent sidebar chat history (October 15, 2026), team-wide chat functionality (October 13, 2026), and ready-made agent teams (September 2026).
verdict: Agentmash offers a highly practical solution for managing AI agent collisions in collaborative environments, though its effectiveness is best realized with a full team rather than individual testing. The generous free tier allows teams to trial the collision detection before committing to a paid plan.

name: bough
description: bough is an open-source tool that reads the local history logs of coding agents like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Pi to visualize project work as a diagram of days, tasks, and prompts. It calculates the cost of individual tasks based on published API rates and helps developers understand where their time and budget were spent.
keyFeatures: Visualizes coding history as a diagram of days, tasks, and prompts
Calculates costs per task based on token usage and published API rates
Provides interactive filters to search prompts, find files, and set spend thresholds
Offers a terminal-based output mode for text-based analysis or JSON data export
Operates entirely offline on the local machine with no external data transmission
bestFor: Developers who use coding agents heavily and need to track the cost of specific features, refactors, or debugging sessions rather than just aggregate monthly totals.
notIdealFor: Users who need live monitoring of active sessions, forecasting against usage limits, or an end-to-end searchable conversation browser.
recentUpdates: Version 0.8.0 added a home page view for all projects, support for custom project naming, and the ability to move between project cards without restarting the tool.
verdict: An essential, privacy-focused utility for power users of AI coding agents who want to gain granular financial and structural insight into their historical work.

name: gitfold
pricingDetail: Free
description: gitfold is a FUSE-based filesystem for Linux that mounts git branches and commits as folders without requiring a full checkout. It provides lightweight, copy-on-write workspaces that allow coding agents and developers to manage multiple branch environments side by side on large monorepos with near-native performance.
keyFeatures: Mount any git revision or branch as a folder in under a second
Linked git worktrees compatible with standard git commands and editors
Copy-on-write storage that only saves modified files
Automatic branch dependency tracking and merged views
Conflict detection and real-time notifications for multiple workspaces
bestFor: Managing dozens of isolated working copies for parallel coding agents or code reviews on large monorepos where standard checkouts are too slow or disk-intensive.
notIdealFor: Build-heavy tasks where high-frequency file I/O performance is critical, or workflows requiring Git LFS, git submodules, or .gitattributes filtering.
recentUpdates: The project was introduced to the public on 2026-11-22 via a Show HN post, highlighting its core capability to serve as a VFS for local git repositories without needing to fetch objects lazily from remote servers.
verdict: An efficient, specialized tool for power users and coding agents on Linux that drastically reduces the disk and time overhead of managing many simultaneous git worktrees.

name: Visual Studio Code
pricingDetail: Free (Individual developers can access the GitHub Copilot Free plan with monthly allowances; paid plans are available for expanded access or enterprise needs).
description: Visual Studio Code is a free, extensible code editor that provides built-in tools for debugging, task running, and version control. It integrates AI-powered assistance for code generation, chat, and task orchestration, allowing developers to work manually or alongside AI agents.
keyFeatures: Integrated AI agents for task orchestration and code collaboration
Rich language support with IntelliSense and refactoring
Built-in Git integration and terminal
Extensive library of plugins via the Visual Studio Marketplace
Cross-platform support with remote development capabilities
bestFor: Developers seeking a lightweight, highly customizable environment for coding, debugging, and AI-assisted workflows across various programming languages.
notIdealFor: Projects requiring full-scale, out-of-the-box IDE features for enterprise-level complex system architecture, where a full Visual Studio IDE might be preferred.
recentUpdates: Starting November 2026, version 1.147 began deprecating support for macOS Ventura and Sonoma, with version 1.149 serving as the final release for these operating systems. Ongoing updates continue to deepen AI integration in the core repository while maintaining performance.
verdict: A powerful, industry-standard editor that perfectly balances core manual coding tools with modern AI-driven agent workflows, all provided at no cost.

name: Xcode
pricingDetail: Xcode ($0), Apple Developer Program ($99/year), Xcode Cloud 100 ($49.99/month), Xcode Cloud 250 ($99.99/month), Xcode Cloud 1,000 ($399.99/month), Xcode Cloud 10,000 ($3,999.99/month)
description: Xcode is Apple's integrated development environment for building, testing, and distributing apps across all Apple platforms including iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Vision Pro. It features advanced coding assistants, device simulators, and integrated continuous integration tools through Xcode Cloud.
keyFeatures: Coding agents and models from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and GitHub Copilot
Device Hub for integrated simulators and physical device management
Swift Testing framework and XCTest for automated testing
Instruments for real-time app performance profiling
Xcode Cloud for continuous integration and delivery
bestFor: Developers building native applications for Apple ecosystems including iOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS.
notIdealFor: Developers working on Windows or Linux or those targeting non-Apple platforms, as the IDE is exclusive to macOS.
recentUpdates: Xcode 27.3 beta 2 released Nov 16, 2026, featuring GitHub Copilot in public preview and new localization skills. Xcode 27.2 released Oct 29, 2026, introduced a .xcproj JSON project format.
verdict: Xcode is the essential, mandatory IDE for the Apple platform, significantly enhanced in version 27 with robust agentic coding capabilities and cross-model support, making it a powerful modern development environment.

name: JetBrains IDEs
pricingDetail: AI Pro ($10/month or $8.33/month billed annually), AI Ultimate ($30/month or $25/month billed annually)
description: JetBrains IDEs integrate advanced AI capabilities through the AI Assistant plugin and the newer Air platform for agentic workflows. These tools provide a unified workspace where developers can leverage various AI coding agents while maintaining full control over the codebase using native IDE features like refactoring, debugging, and testing.
keyFeatures: Native integration of coding agents including Junie, Claude Code, and Codex
In-editor code completion powered by JetBrains proprietary Mellum model
Air workspace for managing parallel agent sessions with Git worktrees
Context-aware AI actions for refactoring, issue detection, and documentation
MCP support for connecting agents to external databases, APIs, and file systems
bestFor: Developers who need to integrate agentic AI workflows while maintaining strict control, auditability, and deep IDE-level verification of generated code.
notIdealFor: Developers seeking an AI-only environment that automates code production without the need for manual review, debugging, or project-wide code understanding.
recentUpdates: Released Air in the 2026.3 update, providing a specialized workspace for managing multiple AI agent sessions, code reviews, and terminal-based agent interactions.
verdict: JetBrains provides a highly professional, transparent approach to AI integration that excels at keeping the developer in control, effectively bridging the gap between autonomous agent output and high-quality, maintainable software engineering.

name: Visual Studio
pricingDetail: Community (Free), Professional monthly ($45/month), Professional standard ($99.99/month), Professional IDE standalone ($499/once), Enterprise monthly ($250/month), Enterprise standard ($499.92/month)
description: Visual Studio is a powerful, Windows-only integrated development environment designed for .NET, C++, and desktop application development. It serves as an AI-native IDE that integrates advanced coding assistance, debugging, and cloud-based deployment tools directly into the development workflow.
keyFeatures: AI-powered coding assistance with Copilot Chat and agent modes
Bring Your Own Key for custom AI model integration
Integrated profiling, debugging, and diagnostic tools
Comprehensive support for .NET, C++, and cross-platform mobile development
Seamless Azure and GitHub integration
bestFor: .NET, C++, and Windows desktop or game development projects.
notIdealFor: Developers working on macOS or Linux, or teams requiring a cross-platform editor.
recentUpdates: The November 2026 update (18.12.1) introduced a rebuilt Copilot Chat based on the Copilot SDK, native AI support for resolving Git merge conflicts, and AI-driven pull request review grouping.
verdict: It remains the most comprehensive toolset for Windows-based software development, though users should be prepared to manage separate costs for Copilot and navigate complex subscription licensing.

name: Copperhead
pricingDetail: CLI (Free), Cloud ($49/user/month), Team ($49/user/month + $199/month platform fee), Enterprise (Custom annual)
description: Copperhead is an open-source, verification-first AI agent designed for printed circuit board (PCB) development using KiCad. It acts as an autonomous assistant that edits schematic and layout files, updates documentation, and verifies designs by running KiCad's own ERC and DRC checks.
keyFeatures: Autonomous PCB design and modification via natural language prompts
Continuous verification using native KiCad ERC/DRC checks
Drift detection to ensure consistency across schematics, BOMs, and documentation
Model-agnostic backend supporting Claude and GPT-5
Git-integrated workflow with automated snapshots and rollbacks
bestFor: Hardware engineers working in KiCad who need to automate design iterations, ensure documentation remains in sync with hardware changes, and maintain strict design constraints.
notIdealFor: Users requiring support for proprietary EDA tools other than KiCad, or those looking for a fully automated autorouter, as Copperhead focuses on verification-gated design rather than layout optimization.
recentUpdates: As of November 12, 2026, Copperhead announced it is open to everyone with billing disabled and free credits for experimentation, including new support for design imports and AI-powered design verification, with Altium import in beta.
verdict: Copperhead is a highly effective, transparent tool for hardware teams looking to treat PCB design like software development, prioritizing design integrity and requirement-gated workflows over traditional manual design processes.

name: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR)
description: NVIDIA Personal AI Router (PAIR) is a local inference tool that connects multiple computers on your network into a cluster to distribute concurrent AI inference workloads. It functions as a proxy that routes requests to available nodes, allowing users to leverage idle hardware without modifying their existing AI applications.
keyFeatures: Workload-aware routing for independent inference requests
Support for Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and vLLM engines
Mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption for secure inter-node communication
Compatibility with OpenAI and Anthropic Messages API formats
Unified management via desktop and terminal interfaces
bestFor: Multi-agent AI workflows and concurrent inference tasks that benefit from distributing parallel requests across multiple local machines.
notIdealFor: Large models requiring pooled GPU memory, requests that must span multiple GPUs, or single, highly sequential tasks where individual request latency is the primary concern.
recentUpdates: Version 1.0.0 (October 2026) introduced native llama.cpp support, validation for RTX Spark hardware, a redesigned terminal interface with a dedicated Jobs tab, and added Anthropic Messages API routing.
verdict: An excellent tool for power users looking to maximize idle local compute for parallel AI tasks, provided they have multiple compatible machines on a trusted network.

name: WebLLM
description: WebLLM is a high-performance, in-browser language model inference engine that leverages WebGPU for hardware acceleration. It enables developers to run open-weights LLMs directly on the client side without server-side processing, ensuring data privacy and offline capability.
keyFeatures: In-browser inference using WebGPU acceleration
Full OpenAI API compatibility (streaming, JSON mode, seeding)
Support for models like Llama, Phi, Gemma, Mistral, and Qwen
Web Worker and Service Worker support for background execution
Custom model integration via MLC format
bestFor: Privacy-focused web applications, offline-capable AI tools, and browser extensions that require local execution without server infrastructure.
notIdealFor: Applications requiring massive frontier models (e.g., 14B+ parameters) that exceed local browser VRAM, high-traffic apps sensitive to CDN egress costs, or environments using WebGL-heavy UI elements prone to GPU stalls.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.89 added support for MiniCPM5, SmolLM3, and LFM2.5 models and exposed tokenization through engine APIs. Version 0.2.88 improved streaming prompt echoes and logprobs. Version 0.2.87 updated model binaries and runtime configurations.
verdict: A robust, high-performance engine for local browser-based LLM inference, ideal for privacy-centric projects, though developers must carefully manage model load sizes and potential GPU resource contention.

name: Magnitude
description: Magnitude is an open-source inference engine that automatically tunes kernels to specific local hardware for optimized performance. It runs as a desktop application and CLI tool, focusing on high-speed inference for coding agents.
keyFeatures: On-device kernel tuning for hardware optimization
Built-in speculative decoding with optimized drafters
Quantized KV cache for reduced memory usage
One-click integration with popular coding agents
Cross-platform support for Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD, and CPUs
bestFor: Developers running local coding agents on Apple Silicon or NVIDIA hardware who need high-performance, low-latency inference.
notIdealFor: Users needing models outside the curated family catalog, those with older hardware, or engineers requiring enterprise-grade headless deployments.
recentUpdates: As of November 2026, the engine is in a transition period; version 0.3.0 alpha releases are currently in development as part of a v4 architectural rewrite, following engine v3 and a catalog update in October 2026.
verdict: Magnitude is a sophisticated, high-performance engine for local coding agents that excels due to its per-device kernel compilation, though its performance gains are highly hardware-dependent and it is currently better suited for specific supported model families than for general-purpose use.

name: text-to-cad
pricingDetail: Free (Free)
description: text-to-cad is an open-source plugin and skills library that enables coding agents to generate 3D models and manufacturing files directly from text or image prompts. It integrates with agents like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot to produce STEP, STL, 3MF, and GLB files using local Python workflows.
keyFeatures: Generation of STEP, GLB, STL, 3MF, and DXF files
Automated manufacturing, stress, and DFM checks
Robot simulation support via URDF, SRDF, and MJCF
Automatic generation of engineering drawings and photorealistic renders
Integration with fabrication services like SendCutSend and Bambu Studio
bestFor: Developers, robotics engineers, and makers who use terminal-based coding agents and require manufacturable 3D models or robot simulations without leaving their environment.
notIdealFor: Users requiring a standalone GUI CAD application, those who need constrained parametric assemblies, or teams that require professional support SLAs and multi-user collaboration.
recentUpdates: Recent versions (v0.11.15-v0.11.17) introduced plugin install fixes, sheet check improvements, CAD engine performance optimizations, and unified community app credits.
verdict: The most comprehensive open-source solution for bringing CAD capabilities to coding agents, offering a robust bridge between LLM-generated code and physical manufacturing.

name: nanochat
pricingDetail: Free (MIT License); users must pay for their own GPU compute, with reference runs costing approximately $15–$48 depending on cloud provider and spot instance usage.
description: nanochat is a minimal, hackable, and educational harness for training large language models from scratch, covering the full pipeline from tokenization and pretraining to reinforcement learning and inference. It is designed to be readable and compact, allowing users to train compute-optimal models with a single complexity dial.
keyFeatures: End-to-end training pipeline including pretraining, SFT, and RL
Single --depth parameter for automated hyperparameter tuning
Public leaderboard for time-to-GPT-2 training speed
Built-in evaluations and inference CLI
Minimal, readable codebase designed for research and learning
bestFor: Developers, researchers, and students who want to study or experiment with the end-to-end mechanics of LLM training.
notIdealFor: Building production-grade assistants, as models are experimental and prone to frequent hallucinations.
recentUpdates: Throughout early 2026, development focused on pretraining optimization, reducing GPT-2-grade training times to 1.65 hours. July 2026 commits added inference benchmarking, tests, and a hardened execution sandbox.
verdict: An exceptional, hands-on educational reference for understanding the modern LLM stack, intended for training and research rather than commercial deployment.

name: colibri
pricingDetail: colibri is free and open-source under the Apache-2.0 license with no paid tiers; the project accepts optional donations. You only need your own hardware (8 GB RAM minimum, 16 GB or more recommended, plus disk space for model weights).
description: colibri is a pure-C inference engine that runs very large mixture-of-experts open models on ordinary computers by keeping the always-active weights in RAM and streaming experts from disk as the model needs them. A one-step setup recommends a model for your machine, builds or downloads the engine and serves OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints that coding agents can use.
keyFeatures: Expert streaming from disk so hundreds-of-billions-parameter MoE models run in modest RAM
CPU, Vulkan and CUDA backends with an optional GPU
Runs published GGUF files as-is, from IQ1_S to Q8_0, F16, BF16 and MXFP4
OpenAI-compatible /v1 and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for coding agents
One-step start-here setup with hardware profiling, model recommendation, resumable downloads and a coli ui dashboard
bestFor: Developers who want to run frontier-scale open MoE models such as GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi or Qwen locally for private coding-agent work without buying datacenter GPUs.
notIdealFor: Latency-sensitive production serving or dense models, since streaming experts from disk trades speed for memory and throughput depends heavily on disk and RAM bandwidth.
recentUpdates: v2.1.0 (October 31, 2026) added native GGUF support on every engine, Mistral-Large-4, Muse Spark Open, Flint and LFM3-VL, CUDA device chains, speculative decoding via MTP heads, 262k-token contexts for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and a new chat UI; v2.0.0 shipped October 6, 2026.
verdict: An impressively compact way to run giant open MoE models on consumer hardware, with agent-ready APIs that make it a practical local backend for coding agents if you can accept disk-bound speeds.

name: FreeToken
description: FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed to run frontier-scale open-weight models on consumer hardware. It optimizes inference by treating the GPU, CPU, and host memory as a unified, elastic platform to handle models that exceed VRAM capacity.
keyFeatures: Bandwidth-adaptive CPU-GPU co-execution with global LRU expert caching
Speculative decoding (MTP and DFlash)
Semantic anchor checkpoints for efficient agentic context reuse
Dynamic VRAM rebalancing between expert and KV caches
OpenAI and Anthropic-compatible API endpoints
bestFor: Developers with NVIDIA gaming or workstation GPUs who need to run large, sparse MoE models locally for agentic coding and tool-calling workloads.
notIdealFor: Users on Apple Silicon, AMD hardware (currently experimental), or those seeking a mature, long-stable stack, as the project is fast-moving and targets NVIDIA infrastructure.
recentUpdates: Version 0.2.3 (November 23, 2026) introduced Gemma-4 MTP speculative drafting, fp8/int8 per-token head KV cache quantization, and DeepSeek-V4.1 GGUF support.
verdict: A high-performance, research-backed local server that effectively bridges the gap between massive MoE models and consumer-grade hardware, making it a powerful backend for technical agent workflows.

name: llama-modchip
pricingDetail: Free (Free to use)
description: llama-modchip is a set of specialized ggml and llama.cpp kernel patches, quantization transcoders, and runtime tools designed to enable high-performance inference of massive mixture-of-experts models entirely on system RAM. It features unique quantization methods like Fractal-64 and Fractal-MXFP4 to fit large models on consumer workstations and includes an agentic SSE gateway for tools like Claude Code.
keyFeatures: Fractal-64 and Fractal-MXFP4 quantization for running 284B models in 64GB RAM
RouteCrack 2.0 speculative engine with N-gram drafting and SIMD micro-arbitration
Persistent /dev/shm KV slot snapshots for near-instant context restoration
Unified modchip CLI for setup, live telemetry, benchmarking, and agentic workflows
Optimized SIMD kernels for AVX-512, AVX2, ARM64 NEON, and Apple Metal
bestFor: Developers with 64GB RAM workstations who need to run large, private open-weights MoE models as a backend for coding agents like Claude Code.
notIdealFor: Users seeking stock compatibility with standard llama.cpp, Ollama, or LM Studio, as the project requires its own patched binaries and specific GGUF formats.
recentUpdates: Version 3.2.0 released in November 2026 introduced an upstream llama.cpp rebase (b12604), quantized heterogeneous Split-KV decode, and native C++ Chained-Prefix HARP-Cache v2 for rapid context restoration.
verdict: An ambitious, high-performance CPU-first MoE runtime that makes massive models accessible on standard hardware, though it is currently best used as an experimental tool given its frequent patching and reliance on custom binaries.

name: Flide
pricingDetail: Apache License 2.0 (Free)
description: Flide is a high-performance inference engine specifically engineered for Jev-style decision models. It utilizes exact state forking to achieve up to 9.5 times faster inference than standard serving engines while ensuring each question is answered as if it were asked in isolation.
keyFeatures: Exact state forking for shared-state multi-question inference
Support for a wide variety of decision model families and chat models (Qwen3.5, Gemma 4)
API compatibility with vLLM and SGLang using the /v1/systemone endpoint
Session cache for resuming agent steps from exact states
Batch-invariant mode to ensure consistent outputs regardless of batching
bestFor: High-throughput decision inference and agent workflows requiring exact state consistency across multiple questions or steps.
notIdealFor: Systems without NVIDIA GPU hardware, or environments requiring non-Linux/non-WSL2 operating systems.
recentUpdates: Version 0.1.20 added Gemma 4 agent sessions (2026-11-23); version 0.1.19 introduced Copernicus-31B, liquamen, Logits-Sigma-1, and turion-jev-31b support along with Docker image availability (2026-11-22).
verdict: Flide is the premier open-source infrastructure for teams needing to scale decision model inference with high accuracy and low latency, significantly outperforming general-purpose LLM serving engines in decision-making workloads.
